belief: I can't be trusted or respected because of my reputation.
origins: A past mistake, a family name, rumors, or a label given in youth can follow us in a community. When people have decided who we are, it can seem pointless to try. We may live down to expectations or withdraw.
teaches: Paul was feared by the church after persecuting believers, yet “Barnabas brought him to the apostles and described how Saul had seen the Lord,” and Saul became Paul. Proverbs says, “A good name is more desirable than great riches,” and a good name can be rebuilt through integrity: “He who walks in integrity walks securely.” Peter says, “Conduct yourselves with such honor among the Gentiles that, though they slander you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day He visits us.” Trust is rebuilt over time through changed behavior, and God’s view of us is not set by gossip.
self_statements: Everyone already has their opinion of me.
Nothing I do will change it.
I will always be that person.
errors: Predicting that no one will ever change their mind.
Accepting a label as my identity.
Believing reputation is either good or ruined.
Feeling ashamed and concluding that nothing can change.
questions: What is my reputation, and what part is true, false, or outdated?
Who has seen me change and treated me differently?
What steps could rebuild trust over time?
How did Barnabas help Paul, and who could be a Barnabas for me?
What does God think of me now?
What will I do consistently this month?
truth: A reputation can change over time through consistent integrity, and God knows me better than gossip does. I can own what is true, let go of what is not, and build trust one step at a time.
hw_truths: A good name can be rebuilt.
log: Each week, note one act of consistent integrity.
actions: Write what is true, false, and outdated.
Apologize or make amends where needed.
Ask a respected person to vouch or walk with you.
prayer: Lord, I carry a reputation that weighs on me. Help me own what is true, release what is not, and rebuild trust with integrity. Send me a Barnabas, and remind me You know my heart. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “Walking in integrity, I can rebuild trust one step at a time.”
